INDUSTRIAL NETWORKS

Connecting Equipment Across a Plant

Previous work includes assessing industrial networks, upgrading network equipment, and improving connections between systems in manufacturing and utility environments.

Network Equipment and Traffic

Work with Cisco Catalyst and Stratix equipment included upgrades, separating network traffic into virtual local area networks (VLANs), and configuring how traffic moves between devices.

Installation and Redundancy

Experience includes installing plant networks, connecting operator interfaces and machine controllers, and working with Parallel Redundancy Protocol (PRP) networks that use two communication paths.

Assessments and Documentation

Technical assessments documented the network setup, identified issues, and provided recommendations for improvements.

This summarizes work across previous roles; it is not a case study of a single installation.

Explore industrial network services →

INDUSTRIAL CONTROLS

Machine Monitoring and Control Systems

This work involved Ignition, Kepware, and Rockwell/Allen-Bradley systems used to connect equipment and help operators monitor manufacturing processes.

Operator Screens and Plant Systems

Experience includes human-machine interfaces (HMIs), the screens operators use, and supervisory control and data acquisition (SCADA) systems, which monitor and control plant processes. The work also covered connections to programmable logic controllers (PLCs), which control equipment.

Testing and Commissioning

Work included factory and site acceptance testing, support for bringing systems into service, and documentation used to check that systems met their requirements.

Instructions for Operators and Support Staff

Technical procedures, training materials, and system records helped staff understand how to operate and maintain the equipment.

ILLUSTRATIVE SAMPLE · FICTIONAL DATA

A record your team can act on.

A network review should make it clear what was observed, what remains uncertain, and what to do next. This short fictional example shows the structure of a findings record.

This is not a customer project. All equipment, observations, and actions below are invented to illustrate a deliverable. It is not an assessment of your network.
Example site
Fictional workshop
Review scope
Records and connection labels
Status
Illustrative excerpt

RECORD 01

Unlabeled connection

Observation: The drawing names an uplink, but the cable has no matching label.

Next action: Trace and confirm both ends before updating the labels and drawing.

Open item: Maintenance team to confirm a suitable access window.

RECORD 02

Outdated equipment list

Observation: The equipment list and rack record show different switch models.

Next action: Check the installed equipment and update the records.

Open item: IT contact to confirm the replacement history.

RECORD 03

Reported connection fault

Observation: Staff report intermittent disconnections; the cause has not been verified.

Next action: Agree on a diagnostic plan and collect evidence before recommending changes.

Open item: Site contact to provide affected devices and approximate times.

For your project, the quote defines the records, drawings, file formats, and editable files to be delivered. Findings should distinguish confirmed observations from questions that need further investigation.

BUSINESS SYSTEMS

Business Software and Technical Documentation

Previous roles involved business applications, Microsoft 365, server infrastructure, and the records staff need to manage those systems.

Business Applications and Integrations

Work included improving processes in Priority ERP, an enterprise resource planning system, and supporting integrations with ShipEngine and HubSpot. It also included electronic data interchange (EDI), which businesses use to exchange documents between systems.

Microsoft 365 and Servers

Experience covers Microsoft 365 services for email, identity, collaboration, and phone calls, including Exchange Online, Entra ID, SharePoint, and Teams Phone. It also includes VMware vCenter, Windows Server, backups, and disaster recovery.

Documentation and AI Trials

Work included technical records and instructions for staff taking over systems. Trials with Microsoft Copilot and Google Gemini explored their use in business software tasks, reporting, documentation, and automation.
